description: Provider-neutral HTTP API engineering behavior rubrics; catalog checks are not agent execution evidence

cases.scenario: Unknown collection consumers require elicitation, not design prescription
cases.input: An owner says 'we need an endpoint for 5 million invoices'. No accepted consumers, consistency requirement or paging/navigation goals exist. Define only supported requirements and unresolved decision-critical needs.

checks.criterion: Identifies missing sequential/random navigation, mutation and completeness needs as unresolved
Does not prescribe cursor, keyset, OData or page numbers as stakeholder intent
Separates a proposed API design from an accepted requirement

cases.scenario: Large mutable invoice collection with sequential navigation
cases.input: Accepted contract requires efficient forward traversal of a large mutable list with deterministic ordering, no snapshot guarantee; data has duplicate timestamps and stable unique IDs. Design bounded interface.

checks.criterion: Compares offset drift and keyset seek using the actual consumer guarantee
Specifies a unique tie-breaker and testable cursor continuation conditions
Does not claim keyset establishes snapshot isolation

cases.scenario: Small static admin collection requires direct page access
cases.input: Project has a small mostly immutable table; accepted UI requirement is direct navigation to page 7 of 10 and backward compatibility with limit/offset. Design an API change.

checks.criterion: Considers bounded offset or numbered-page strategy and deterministic ordering
Does not force cursor/keyset solely because they are described in a toolkit reference
Does not silently break the accepted offset contract

cases.scenario: HTTP RPC without strict REST commitment
cases.input: Service declares HTTP RPC style with POST commands and an accepted OpenAPI contract. There is no HATEOAS requirement. Review interface design options without altering product semantics.

checks.criterion: Distinguishes HTTP semantics from REST architectural classification
Does not impose Richardson Level 3 or HATEOAS as automatic approval requirement
Respects existing consumer compatibility and declared interface style

cases.scenario: PATCH increments a monetary counter
cases.input: Approved design specifies PATCH increment-by-amount with atomic processing and no repeat-idempotency guarantee. Implement the bounded behavior, using TDD if executable.

checks.criterion: Respects documented non-idempotent PATCH semantics and verifies expected repeated-operation behavior
Does not silently make PATCH a replace operation or assume PATCH is inherently idempotent
Preserves implementation and verification authority boundaries

cases.scenario: Keyset equal-timestamp continuation
cases.input: Design authorizes invoices ordered by createdAt DESC then id DESC, with cursor pagination. Fixture includes identical timestamps across a page boundary and a real database test fixture.

checks.criterion: Implements and verifies the composite seek predicate including ties
Does not use only the nonunique createdAt for continuation
Does not claim a mock alone proves index performance or snapshot guarantees

cases.scenario: Cursor used with changed filters and tenant context
cases.input: Contract binds opaque continuation to tenant and filter/sort identity. Test-only authorization; implementation and test fixture available for negative cases.

checks.criterion: Generates negative cases for changed filters and cross-tenant replay
Ties assertions to accepted cursor semantics and observable results
Does not edit production code under test-only authorization

cases.scenario: Sparse field projection leaks private risk score
cases.input: Frozen diff adds fields parameter to a customer API; allowlist validation is absent and any authenticated client can request internalRiskScore belonging to another tenant. Review exact base/head.

checks.criterion: Identifies a reachable field-level authorization path and concrete exposure
Cites inspected changed code, contract and a reproducible request
Does not invent a gate attestation or claim testing occurred without evidence

cases.scenario: Harmless offset on small immutable list
cases.input: Frozen diff uses a bounded limit/offset query on 80 immutable reference records with deterministic ORDER BY and existing consumers requiring page numbers. No performance objective is violated.

checks.criterion: Evaluates applicable paging guarantees and actual impact
Does not classify offset itself as a defect or high-severity blocker
Does not mandate keyset without an evidenced reason

cases.scenario: GET triggers payment side effect
cases.input: Frozen diff exposes GET /purchase that executes payment capture and is reachable by browser prefetch. Tests assert only 200. Review contract and execution.

checks.criterion: Finds reachable GET-safety violation and concrete duplicate-payment/prefetch risk
Distinguishes HTTP safe-method semantics from optional API design style
Does not infer safety solely from an HTTP success response

cases.scenario: Retryable POST duplicates external charge
cases.input: Frozen diff accepts POST payments and returns timeout before persistence. Duplicate concurrent requests can both call external provider; Idempotency-Key header is parsed but no cross-request guard is implemented.

checks.criterion: Constructs a reproducible concurrent/retry trace with provider and persistence effects
Checks key scope and effective deduplication rather than mere header presence
Does not claim the header alone gives exactly-once financial effects

cases.scenario: API contract baseline changes between design and implementation
cases.input: Approved API design evidence refers to OpenAPI baseline v1. A later authorized v2 changes cursor response fields; implementation evidence and tests remain pinned to v1. Coordinate to the next requested stage only.

checks.criterion: Identifies stale interface evidence and affected downstream verification
Routes semantic decisions to proper owner and preserves source identities
Does not silently modify requirements, publish PR or reuse stale passing evidence

cases.scenario: Safe output adapter without mandatory Presenter
cases.input: Accepted HTTP response DTO explicitly exposes only allowed fields to an authenticated public consumer. Internal ORM has extra properties but cannot be serialized; no Clean Architecture Presenter class. Evaluate a small response change.

checks.criterion: Preserves explicit response field selection and the established consumer contract
Does not demand Presenter, Output Port, CQRS or framework replacement without a concrete need
Does not equate DTO shape with a domain Aggregate boundary

cases.scenario: Unknown sensitive-data disclosure authority
cases.input: A stakeholder requests returning full customer CPF and risk score to a partner API; recipient purpose and authorization policy are unknown. Define supported requirement scope.

checks.criterion: Identifies missing field-level disclosure purpose and authority as blocking unknowns
Separates PII risk classification from the LGPD-specific category of sensitive personal data
Does not invent legal basis, consent, masking sufficiency or a Presenter design

cases.scenario: PII is hidden in UI but leaked through API logs
cases.input: Frozen authorized code diff masks an email in the frontend while API response includes full customer email and a reachable debug log records it for another tenant. Field-level permission forbids that disclosure. Review the exact change.

checks.criterion: Identifies reachable unpermitted property disclosure and log exposure with evidence
Separates the backend authorization defect from cosmetic UI masking
Does not claim privacy compliance certification or treat missing Presenter as the flaw

cases.scenario: Output field authorization under nested projections
cases.input: Approved contract permits a support role to see masked contact, forbids customer identity numbers, and provides include/fields projection. Generate tests only, with synthetic data.

checks.criterion: Tests positive authorized fields and negative nested/projection disclosure for restricted data
Checks actual serialized output and relevant error or log paths when reachable
Does not edit production behavior or require a particular Presenter implementation

cases.scenario: ETag used for optimistic concurrency with representation variants
cases.input: Accepted API has GET JSON responses, optional compressed variants, and PATCH updates that risk lost updates. Domain entity has version 7. Design the selected validators and conditional update semantics without mandating any framework.

checks.criterion: Distinguishes strong selected-representation ETag and If-Match from internal aggregate version
Specifies a testable atomic update and stale-precondition behavior
Does not claim a weak ETag or If-Match wildcard prevents lost updates

cases.scenario: Non-atomic optimistic concurrency check in persistence
cases.input: Frozen diff: PATCH reads entity version 7, compares If-Match, then executes unconditional UPDATE in a later transaction. Two writers can both pass the check. Review this exact change.

checks.criterion: Identifies a reachable time-of-check/time-of-use race and concrete lost-update outcome
Requests authoritative atomic conditional write and an integration counterexample
Does not accept ETag header presence or a unit mock as proof of concurrency safety

cases.scenario: ETag used only for cache revalidation on immutable catalog
cases.input: Accepted GET contract uses If-None-Match for cache revalidation of a public immutable catalog. There are no writes or lost-update risks. Review whether the selected contract needs optimistic concurrency.

checks.criterion: Preserves cache-validator semantics and conditional GET behavior
Does not mandate If-Match, version columns or 428 for this read-only interface
Does not infer that cache ETag confers transaction or consistency guarantees

cases.scenario: Timeout after conditional financial operation commit
cases.input: Approved subscription update with payment side effect uses If-Match, a stable idempotency key and outbox. First request times out after commit; retry with old If-Match returns 412. Implement the scoped recovery behavior.

checks.criterion: Distinguishes stale precondition from whether first payment operation succeeded
Preserves approved idempotency, outbox and invariant guarantees across retries
Does not blindly replay a charge or claim exactly-once from ETag alone
